records.text: Push authority to the smallest accountable unit. Escalate only irreversible bets; record the owner, evidence, and reversal cost.
AI-native teams work best as small stable groups with end-to-end outcomes instead of functional handoffs and approval queues.
Governance should separate reversible experiments from high-consequence commitments. Fast local moves need clear rollback and decision logs.
Agents can propose and execute bounded work, while people own purpose, risk tolerance, and irreversible commitments.
The first learning session should deliver a small visible success before setup or curriculum depth, so beginners feel capable immediately.
A progressive curriculum should unlock the next challenge after demonstrated confidence, not expose the full map up front.
Explain agent systems through outcomes, examples, and plain language before introducing architecture vocabulary.
Healthy learning communities show returning participation, peer help, completed experiments, and members sharing what they built.
A saved source bundle containing independent resources for later recall.
